items.title: Goldman: hedge funds sold the rip, tech long/short at a record low
items.summary: Goldman's latest prime-services data show professional managers covering index hedges while continuing to sell individual stocks, and pushing technology long/short exposure to the lowest level in the bank's records, even as the index rally made the selling look mistimed.

items.title: BoA: risk-off stays in place as the dollar leads
items.summary: The Nov 12 bank note keeps a tactical risk-off stance. The BoA Bull & Bear Indicator is at 7.4, up from 7.2, with the equity-flow component at the 96th percentile (very bullish) and fund-manager positioning at the 100th percentile (very bullish), while global stock-index breadth is at the 21st percentile (bearish). Weekly global equity fund inflows were $98.3 billion, the largest since June 2026. Year-to-date, US stocks are about +10.9% and the dollar about +4.9%. The November fund manager cash and crowded-trade survey is not yet the basis for the site's Soft ↔ Crowded fund-manager panel, which is still the August 2026 survey.

items.title: Desk market wrap 11/9
items.summary: Stocks bounced to start the week as oil dropped another 3% and eased inflation fears, though AI financing stayed an overhang. SPY and QQQ squeezed back to the 8-day average on a wide-range session; desk waits on this week's inflation data. A few large call books adjusted.

items.title: Desk open wrap 11/9
items.summary: Futures firmer to start the week as oil kept falling and metals bid; VIX dropped again. Europe recovered some of last week's losses and Nikkei bounced after last week's slide. CPI is next.
